options: A script that reverses exactly what a specific up-migration did
A migration that only runs on lower-numbered database versions
A backup taken before any migration runs
A script that reduces the size of a table's indexes
questions.explain: Pairing an up-migration with a down-migration gives the pipeline a scripted way to reverse a specific change.

questions.q: Under what condition is a down-migration for adding then dropping a column considered safe and symmetric?
options: As long as nothing has started depending on that column's data yet
Only if the column is nullable
Always, regardless of how much data has accumulated
Only if the table has fewer than 100 rows
questions.explain: Symmetry holds only while no real, meaningful data depends on the change — once it does, reversal risks real data loss.

questions.q: Why would running a down-migration to drop a column be the wrong move after real order data has accumulated in it?
options: It would destroy real data that now exists because of decisions made after the migration ran, not just undo a schema change
SQL Server technically refuses to drop any column that has ever contained data
It would have no effect at all on the live database
Down-migrations can only be run once per environment, ever
questions.explain: Once real data depends on a change, 'rolling back' the schema is really a data-loss decision, not a clean mechanical reversal.

options: Deploying a new migration that corrects a problem going forward, rather than attempting to reverse a migration that already touched live data
Refusing to ever fix any migration mistake
Manually editing the database through SSMS instead of using migrations
Reverting the entire database to a backup taken before the mistake
questions.explain: Forward-fix-only applies the same additive migration principle: correct problems with new migrations rather than rewriting history.

questions.q: When should the team decide whether a migration has a clean rollback path or requires forward-fix-only, per this lesson?
options: During code review, before the migration is ever deployed — not discovered during an actual incident
Only after a production incident has already occurred
Rollback strategy never needs to be decided in advance
Automatically, by a tool that requires no human judgment
questions.explain: A reviewer should flag whether a migration has a clean rollback or needs forward-fix-only before it ever merges.
